featured_reviews.name: vivek kapoor
featured_reviews.review_text:
My visit to this temple left me in awe and peace. I am told the temple is almost 6 decades old and has been developed over a period of time. It started with a deity and then led to the others. What immediately strikes you is the way they have tried to maintain a similarity in the look and feel of the place. Most places land up looking very disjointed due to varied styles over a period of time. Not this temple. The deities are lined up in a sequence, making it easy for a person to do all the darshan. There is Ganesh, Ramji, 9 Grahas, etc, all under one roof with a very typical temple architecture associated with South India. There is a small stage, an auditorium also which is housed in the complex. There is an administrative office, too. You feel welcome and not rushed at all and can sit and be one with God as long as you like. Their timings are from 5.30am to 10.30am in the morning and 5.30pm to 9pm. Prasadam is freshly prepared and given to every visitor.
Right at the entrance itself is a shoe rack to keep the footwear in order to maintain the sanctity of the place. There is a flower vendor housed there, too, so all you need to do is go with bhakti in your heart and come back energised with loads of positive energy.

featured_reviews.name: Gayatri Upadhyay
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Sacred Encounter: My Temple Experience

As I stepped onto the temple grounds, a profound silence embraced me. The world outside—filled with its hurried footsteps and restless voices—seemed to fade away, replaced by the gentle rustling of leaves and the distant chime of bells. The scent of incense lingered in the air, wrapping around me like an unseen blessing.

Inside the temple, the golden glow of lamps illuminated the deities, their serene faces reflecting a wisdom beyond time. Devotees knelt in quiet prayer, their whispers merging with the rhythmic chants that echoed through the hall. I closed my eyes and felt the vibrations of those sacred sounds ripple through me, grounding me in the present yet lifting me beyond it.

Kneeling before the altar, I let go of the burdens I had carried here—worries, doubts, unanswered questions. In that moment, the weight of the world seemed lighter. I did not ask for miracles, only clarity. And in the stillness, I found something even greater: a sense of peace.

As I stepped back into the world outside, the experience stayed with me—not as a memory, but as a quiet presence in my heart. The temple had given me more than just a visit; it had gifted me a moment of connection, both with the divine and with myself.

Hinglaj Mata, a form of the Hindu goddess Durga, is revered as a Kuldevi (family deity) by several Hindu communities.
Despite being in the heart of Mumbai, the Hinglaj Mata Temple offers a surprising sense of calm. The hustle and bustle of the city seem distant as you step into this sacred space, and the noise of the streets fades away, replaced by the soothing chants and the gentle hum of prayers. The peaceful atmosphere inside creates a sanctuary where you can connect spiritually, even in the midst of one of India’s busiest urban areas. It feels like a place where the divine meets the everyday, providing solace to those seeking a moment of peace in a hectic world.
The presence of devoted visitors and the rituals being performed give the temple a vibrant spiritual energy. The air is filled with the fragrance of incense, the sound of bell chimes, and the hum of prayers, creating a space where devotion and faith come alive.
The Hinglaj Mata Temple has deep cultural and historical roots, as it is associated with the goddess Hinglaj Mata, who is believed to offer protection and blessings.
Inside, the atmosphere feels meditative and introspective. The simplicity of the temple’s surroundings helps focus the mind on prayer or reflection and perhaps find clarity or guidance.

The rituals, the divine presence, and the peaceful atmosphere all come together to create a memory that stays with you. It’s one of those places where, after you leave, you carry a piece of its serenity with you, making you want to return again.

featured_reviews.name: prajith pradeep
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Divine Confluence of South Indian Traditions and Mumbai’s Spirit!

This is undoubtedly the best Ayyappa temple in Mumbai. Located in the heart of Ghatkopar, it serves as a spiritual landmark where South Indian temple traditions meet the incredible soul and bhakti of Maharashtra.

The Temple Experience:

The Deities: The main shrine of Lord Ayyappa is surrounded by beautiful shrines for Lord Ganapathi and Goddess Durga, creating a complete and powerful atmosphere for prayer.

Weekly Padi Puja: A major highlight is the Padi Puja held every Saturday. It is a magnificent ritual that brings the essence of the 18 holy steps right here to our city.

Best Time to Visit: You must visit during Deeparadhana in the evening. As the diyas (lamps) are lit, the vibe becomes absolutely magical—it is the perfect time for darshan and meditation.

A Local Treasure: What I love most is how the temple brings everyone together. Whether it’s during the festive Mandala season or a regular weekend, you see the local Maharashtrian community and South Indian devotees joining hands in chanting "Swamiye Saranam Ayyappa!" The temple is clean, peaceful, and managed with great discipline.

A truly serene place that offers peace to every Mumbaikar’s soul. 🚩🙏

Gurudev Shree Milan Bawashri and Shree Bantu Bawashree (Dandwat pranam J J) have done us a big favour by bringing us closer to Thakurji and relentlessly assuring in ways possible that our culture, our pride is safeguarded and passed on in its purest form to the present and future generations.

As for the Vraj Yatra 2022, I read someone posting their experience in a derogatory way.

It is often said, “Aagnya ane Adhikaar Layaak jeev ne j male”
Meaning, Only the worthy shall get the Permission and Right (in context to the Parikrama, and staying on the Pavitra Vraj Bhoomi)

The reason someone has to leave the Parikrama midway, means that they lost their worth of completing it… Why they lost their worth, is for them to introspect, think and understand…

While I was not fortunate to be able to attend the Vraj Yatra, my wife with my 4 year old daughter attended the Yatra and completed it without any trouble! For once I didnt ask about their wellbeing coz I was sure that they are safe and sound under J J’s surveillance…

Heavy rains disrupted the Tents, everyone was asked to evacuate the tents but J J and family stayed back to ensure everything was up and in order…

It’s disheartening to know that people are concerned about facilities, food, stay etc when they cant see the bigger privilege of being able to do the Parikrama with J J!

Pratyaksh Gyaan tumhe na milaa,
Anumaan se samaja naa Koi….

The Shirdi Saibaba Temple, located at Shirdi, Maharashtra, India attracts millions of devotees of all religions, castes and creed who come to pay homage to Shri Sai Baba. The temple is a beautiful shrine that was built over the Samadhi of Shri Sai Baba.

Shirdi is a small village in Kopargam taluk, in Ahmadnagar District of the Maharastra State. When Baba was physically present at the age of 20 in Shirdi, Shirdi was a small village of about 70/80 houses of mud walls. Today Shirdi is a big town with modern buildings, hotels, lodges and shops.

Thursday is the day Saibaba is specially worshipped. On this day devotees from all over India visit Shirdi for Darshan of Saibaba.

Sai temple shirdi opens for devotees at 5.15 a.m. (0515 hrs) with Kakad Aarti and remains open till the end of Shejarti.

featured_reviews.name: The Chartered Traveller
featured_reviews.review_text:
Usually, you have to get down from the car on the main road itself, as vehicles cannot directly go till the temple. From there, you need to walk around 400 meters and then climb around 50-100 stairs to reach the temple.

The temple is one of the most famous temples in Mumbai and is dedicated to Maa Mahalakshmi, Maa Mahakali, and Maa Mahasaraswati. It is believed that during the construction of the Hornby Vellard project, the work kept failing due to sea disturbances. Later, the idols of the goddesses were found in the sea and installed here, after which the project was completed successfully. Since then, devotees believe the temple brings blessings and prosperity.

When we visited, there were only around 10-15 people, so we got darshan almost instantly, in less than a minute. It felt very peaceful and amazing. We bought flowers from outside and offered them inside the temple.

One important thing, currently there is no proper shoe stand available. People there said one is under construction, so for now you either have to buy prasad from shops outside and keep footwear there, or keep them at your own risk.

After darshan, just beside the temple downstairs, there is a beautiful Hanuman temple, and another small temple opposite to it, both worth visiting.

Overall, within around 15 minutes, we completed everything peacefully. It’s a very nice and peaceful temple with calm positive vibes and good seating space.

featured_reviews.name: Shyam Nair
featured_reviews.review_text:
Shri Mahalakshmi Devi Temple, Mumbai is one of Mumbai's most prominent and historic places of worship, highly revered for its spiritual energy and beautiful seaside setting. Dedicated to the Tridevi—Goddess Mahalakshmi, Goddess Mahakali, and Goddess Mahasaraswati—the temple provides a deeply serene yet bustling environment for devotees.
Visitors frequently highlight several aspects of their experience in their reviews:
* **Atmosphere & Divine Experience:** Reviewers consistently mention the powerful, positive vibrations and peaceful energy they feel upon entering the complex. The main idols are beautifully adorned with gold ornaments and traditional jewelry, which many describe as a breathtaking and spiritually moving sight.
* **Crowd & Queue Management:** As a highly popular destination, the temple sees massive footfall. While there are separate, systematic lines for men and women that often move quickly during regular hours, crowd management can become a challenge during peak times. Reviewers note that queues can spill out onto the connecting roads, and some suggest that better shade and permanent railings on the approaching paths would improve the waiting experience.
* **Best Times to Visit:** Devotees highly recommend visiting on weekdays if you prefer a quieter, more relaxed darshan. Weekends, Tuesdays, and Fridays tend to be significantly more crowded, while the festival of Navaratri draws massive waves of pilgrims, resulting in wait times that can stretch into hours.
* **Amenities & Strict Policies:** The temple complex includes smaller shrines dedicated to other deities and features plenty of stalls right outside selling flowers, coconuts, and sweets for offerings. Visitors remind others that photography and mobile phone use are strictly prohibited inside the main temple area to maintain sanctity.

featured_reviews.name: Vedant Anasune
featured_reviews.review_text: A deeply spiritual and peaceful place in the heart of Mumbai. The temple has a powerful and positive atmosphere that instantly makes you feel calm and connected. The sea view nearby adds to the beauty of the experience, especially during early mornings or evenings. Despite being crowded during festivals and weekends, the darshan is well managed. A must-visit for anyone seeking blessings, peace of mind, and a beautiful devotional vibe in the city.

featured_reviews.name: Vinod K Tripathi
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had the divine opportunity to visit Shree Mahalaxmi Temple, and it was a truly peaceful and spiritually enriching experience.
Located near the Arabian Sea, the temple offers not only religious significance but also a beautiful scenic view. As you approach the temple, the positive energy and devotion of the devotees create a very calming and भक्तिमय atmosphere. Despite being in a busy city like Mumbai, the temple gives a sense of peace and spiritual connection.
The darshan व्यवस्था is quite well managed, although there can be a heavy crowd, especially during weekends and festivals like Navratri. Still, the movement of devotees is systematic, and the temple authorities ensure a smooth experience.
The idol of Maa Mahalaxmi is beautifully decorated, and the feeling during darshan is truly divine. You can feel a deep sense of faith and positivity while standing in front of the goddess.
Cleanliness in and around the temple is well maintained. There are also small shops nearby for पूजा सामग्री, adding to the overall experience.
Overall, visiting Mahalaxmi Temple was a very fulfilling and blessed experience. It is definitely a must-visit for devotees and anyone seeking peace amidst the city’s busy life.
Jai Maa Mahalaxmi 🙏

featured_reviews.name: Ramya Iyer
featured_reviews.review_text:
Very divine environment. The temple is located in Kalbadevi. The temple is dedicated to Balaji. It is constructed in Tamil/ Dravidian style. Moreover, the temple has different sannidhi for devi. Every Saturday or maybe everyday morning, you will get pongal as prasad. Apart from this, you can buy laddoo. The laddoos are very good-yes, those big laddoos-similar to those served in Tirupati Balaji temple in Andhra Pradesh.

How to reach?
1. Get down at CST
2. Take a cab to Fanaswadi or take a bus and get down at Fanaswadi stop.

option 2:
1. Get down at Charni road station
2. The temple is 1kms from the station.

featured_reviews.name: omkar gurudu
featured_reviews.review_text: Sri Venkateswara Balaji Mandir in Mumbai was established in 1927, consecrated by Jagataguru Ananthacharya Swamiji, and is a replica of the Tirumala Venkateswara Temple. Its architecture is a beautiful example of Dravidian style, featuring an impressive Gopuram, a gold-plated Dhwajasthambam (flagstaff), and a Vimana over the sanctum. The temple is known as "Bombay's Little Tirupati" for its devotion to Lord Venkateswara and its observance of traditional Vaishnavite customs.
